cast.say: We HAD 41. You drank one while I counted.
Who let a new one in? I just finished!
I have audited myself. There are discrepancies.
One wagon of goods, three hundred even!
I count 299 goods and one suspicious wagon.
So it SAYS. Four wheels. Like last year. Hm.
Me! Just out for a walk.
It's a NUMBER. Numbers aren't 'a lot.'
Ohhh, strike the earth, the earth, the earth...
In the reprise I stand on a table.
Those were all of my mugs.
I know four hundred songs about trees.

panels.caption: The elf left after song thirty.

cast.say: I can't rest until it ends.
Then I'll sing until we're not.
Hello, neighbour! May I borrow some bones?
He can have mine. I'm not using them.
So sorry! They're learning a song.
Your bard. He only knows the one.
A siege! Shall I tidy that up for you?

panels.caption: A polite flick of the wrist.

cast.say: A pie, to welcome you to the cavern!
Gerald is the pie. Say hello, Gerald.
Could you watch my ghosts this week?
He lets us haunt till midnight!
Ah, but I was dead for most of it.
Then I'll send the borrower who died.
Hi. It's me. I have no coins.
Just covering a quick pump shift!
Any minute now, someone will relieve me.
Oh, that was for my bath. Last winter.
Could someone bring me a drink?
There's a hauling priority for that.
And where am I on it?

cast.think: He's been carrying it a month.

cast.say: Pumping magma up to the forges!
A year of pumping. Feel these arms.
Can't. If I let go, the fort floods.
Last swap was spring. Look how it went.
Heavens, no. The title is 'Pump Baron.'
Odd. The pump just got heavier.
How long have you been in there?
Could we stand in it at the tavern?
...That's just the queue for the bar.
Recruits, welcome to the danger room!
Goblins at the gate! To arms!
We drill on Mondays. We don't fight.
A mug is NOT a weapon!
So the booze stays safe from goblins!
We're keeping it safe in here.
It's a stethoscope that holds ale.
The dog will now scan your bones.
Good news: you have all your bones.
The second opinion agrees. So does the third.
We're out of splints. Have a mug.
For your mood. The leg is on its own.
I get very hairy every full moon.
Now I tap your knee with the mug.
Who threw a mug at me?
Not a tantrum, my lord. A reflex!

gags.caption: "We accept payment in apologies, one per chair you own."
Day one aboveground: the ceiling is too far away and nobody will fix it.
Strange mood requests: one gem, one log, and 'a little privacy, Doris.'
The cats have installed their own door. Nobody remembers approving it.
The forgotten beast would like to be remembered, preferably as 'Steve.'
The hill titan asked for the tavern. We gave him the elves' address.
The kobold's lost and found is thriving. Everything in it is ours.
Roll call: Urist, Urist, Urist. And the new migrant, Urist.
The scholars agree: 'winning' is a myth invented by elves.
{citizen} says every plump helmet has its own personality. Most are 'plump.'
The dining hall is 'legendary' thanks to one engraving of a very nice cheese.
'Dig down,' they said. Nobody ever mentioned when to stop.
He's not a vampire. He just hates sunlight and sleeps where the missing dwarves were.
Week three of the siege. The goblins' tavern is now nicer than ours.
"Is that just a rock?" "It's a ☼rock☼. Notice the little suns."
The line for the well is {pop} dwarves long. The front of it is a cat.
The carp has learned to work the pump. It's pumping the dwarves OUT.
Minecart commute: three seconds. Recovery time: three weeks.
The baron likes his new bedroom, except that it's in the same fort as us.
The scholar's thesis, 'Why Is the Sky?', received peer review: a thrown mug.
Poetry night: twelve odes to wine, one to water, and a brawl about the water one.
{citizen_first} has been upset since the {weather}. The furniture is now upset too.
{artifact} was voted the fort's finest treasure. The dwarf who made it came second.
The ghost wants a memorial slab. The mason wants to see some references.
Carpenter's best seller: the coffin. Second best: the bed, for practice.
Somewhere above the sky, someone clicked 'dig' 400 times. Down here it feels personal.
{dogs} dogs in the fort, and not one will fetch the hammerer.
{drinks} drinks in stock. Rations are now measured in barrels per dwarf per mood.
The elf is hugging the last tree. The woodcutter is hugging his axe. Talks go on.
The tailor no longer asks about the claw marks. He just charges extra.
The baby has survived three sieges and still refuses to eat plump helmets.
We call it an 'open-plan layout.' The engineer calls it 'the cave-in.'
Urist has stood in the rain for an hour 'to see what the fuss is about.'
New wheelbarrows: now one dwarf can move one stone, but more slowly.
Mandate: three ☼crowns☼ by spring. Stock: one crown and one very sweaty jeweler.
Welcome to {fort}. Population {pop}. Elves, please keep going.
